title: Gabriel Schmid in Barcelona
content:
Barcelona Part 2012 Gabriel Schmid:

January in Austria is winter and it isn`t possible to skate outdoor because of the snow and the uncomfortable tempratures.

Yannic (an ambitious filmer from Graz) and I got sick of skating the indoor parks and hanging on the couch, so we decided fly southwards and to get out of the grey austrian winter.

Our destination: Barcelona.

We had an appartement near to the famous rambla which is located very central. The weather was sunny and we had between 15-20 degrees, perfect conditions to skate the endless variety of spanish skate spots.

The lazy winter days were over and we went out for filming missions almost every day and in the evening we had some relaxed skate sessions at macba or parallel.

Yannic was very motivated on filming and always had new ideas for shots and I was hyped to skate everything that came in my way, that in end of that month we had more footage than we had expected.

Check it out for your self here is the clip of Barcelona edited and filmed by Yannic:

title: „Parallel„ the legendary skate spot in Barcelona destroyed:
content:
Since the end of the 90s Barcelona is an important city for skateboarding. There are many spots and the weather is nice, so it´s still a popular travel destination for skateboarders all over the world. Pro skaters came to film for their videos and to shoot photos for magazines. The spot “parallel” was located in the center of the city.

“The atmosphere was relaxed, trees gave shadow on a sunny day, the place was surrounded by walls full of street art and the ground was perfect to have a smooth ride.”

The spot was a good meeting point to start a skate session and to warm up a bit. Even after a day of street skating, going to “parallel” to end your day with some relaxed manuals or to drink some beers and chill with your friends was perfect. It never was officially allowed to skate there but in contrary to other famous spots you hardly got busted by the police or any people who lived nearby. “Parallel” was shown in many skatevideos, for skaters it was popular worldwide.

“A few weeks ago the government of Barcelona started to break it down. They put fences around the place and the first manual pads are already gone.”

Skateboarders were told that the old spot will be replaced by a skatepark. It is pleasant that Barcelona officially allows skateboarders to skate in this area and that the city even wants to improve the place for skaters. The problem is that the spot was part of the skate history; it was a meeting point for skaters all over the world for about two decades. Skateboarders want to use the architecture for their pleasure and that obstacles aren`t built to skate makes them more attractive.

“Parrallel” was so good to skate but still had the street style, so on one hand skaters can be thankful that the city does something for them but on the other hand the government communicated to less with the skaters because if they had, they would know that skaters don´t need a skatepark there.

If the city simply had allowed to skate this place and if they had renovated it, skaters would have been happy. Skateboarders will always remember the legendary “parallel” were some of the most technical tricks have been landed and so many good times were spent.

title: Burek and Karlovacko – Skateboard trip Croatia
content:
Enough of skating our local indoor skatepark. We still had to wait for spring, so we packed Miran´s car and left to Split in Croatia. Our next Skateboard trip:

The crew consisted of Miran, who is Croatian, Joel from Australia, Samuel from Germany, Luki the Austrian, me as half Colombian and Ari, Miran´s baby dog.

The perfect gang for a short skate trip to start in the skate season of 2015. Miran´s Croatian language skills made it much easier for us, he organized a really smooth apartment in the center of the city. After checking in, we were so hyped to skate because it had 15-20 degrees whereas in our hometown we had around 0 degrees. We bought some Karlovackos, that´s the name of a Croatian beer, for snacks some Bureks, this is some Croatian food which made us all addicted, we had a cruise through the city center and little session on the promenade next to the ocean and under the palms. Skateboarding and filming was our main focus of the trip, so the next day we headed early to the local spot to warm up and later to hit some of the plenty street spots in Split.

During our warm up session we met Mario and Leo, two locals who were really nice guys, who brought us to many amazing places in Split and went skating with us every day.

So we could film a lot of stuff, but not without fighting our fears and our legs got sore every day because the spots were big and not easy to skate. Samuel ripped so hard and seemed to know no fear but unfortunately on the third day he had a heel bruise so he wasn´t able to skate for the rest of the trip. At least there are so many beautiful women in Split so he didn´t get bored. One man down and with heavy legs from skating every day the missions went on, so also Luki rolled his ankle and wasn´t able to skate anymore.

From this time we knew we had to keep it mellow, and we concentrated more on the nice weather, the ladies, the ocean, Karlovackos and Bureks.

All together it was an amazing trip and the time passed too fast, i recommend everybody Split as destination for a skate tour. If you want to see more check out the clip of our trip which was made :

title: Skateboarding Trip through Europe
content:
Graz is a quiet and peaceful city to live in. Very relaxed, not so stressful like big cities.

When you are young, you probably do not want to spend your whole time in this comfortable Atmosphere. Exploring new countries, experience many different situations and getting in contact with foreign people appears very interesting.

So I thought about going on a skateboarding trip through southern Europe,Julian and Lucas, two friends of mine, were amazed by the idea so we decided to realize that plan. We packed our most important things, always trying to avoid as mu ch weight as possible, we took our skateboards and we were ready to go. We bought a Train Ticket which allowed us to travel through Europe for one month. Our first destination was Milan because we have heard that there are a lot of skate spots. After a long train ride we arrived at the main station, it was late in the evening and we didn’t know where to sleep. In front of the central station besides of many junkies there is the local skate spot of Milan.We stayed there and had a cool session, so we came in contact with the locals, they showed us a cheap hostel were we could sleep and invited us to skate with them the next day.The locals brought us to many spots and gave us an impression of the urban life in Milan.

At the first look Milan is a shiny and glamours city but at the second look you see a lot of drug addicts and criminality.

From Milan we took the train to Lyon, we spent one night exploring the city without a sleeping place and because the weather was so bad, in the morning we took the first train with direction to Spain. After the Spanish border we got off the train in a little village because someone told us that there are beautiful beaches.

We needed a break from the cities, so we chilled one week on the beach sleeping outside, swimming in the ocean and diving from the rocks.

Next stop was the skate paradise Barcelona where we met some friends from Austria and we had a week of skating the best places every day. Unfortunately Julian rolled his ankle so he was forced to chill, but there are many other ways to have a good time in Barcelona, for example looking at the street art which is on every corner. It was hard to leave Barcelona with it´s perfect spots, the nice weather, the communicative people and the beautiful ladies. Still it was time for Me, Julian and Lucas to leave and we took a high speed train to Madrid. We needed a short break from skateboarding because our legs were sore and Julian still had problems with his ankle so we took a look at the city walking around and meeting interesting people. After two days we wanted to move on to Lisbon where a friend of us was studying. The train was full so we stayed a few more days in Madrid and we had the opportunity to get to know the skatelife in Madrid but it wasn´t that easy because during the day it had 35 degrees. In Lisbon we went to our friends house which was located twenty minutes from the center right next to the beach. Patrick was doing his exchange year there and he lived in a surf house with many other cool people.

We felt as if a dream had become true, the house had a swimming pool and a pool were you could skate in, it was full of young people who were partying a lot and at the beach you could surf and watch beautiful ladies.

Patrick already knew many local skateboarders who were hyped to go skate with us and brought us to so good spots and we had such a great time. In the evenings we grilled and chilled at the poolside or we went to the city center to crash the Portuguese nightlife which is really crazy. Julian and Lucas had to leave after ten days but for me it was to early and I stayed three more weeks in Lisbon. Then I wanted to go to France to meet another friend but I hurt my foot on a skating mission so I wasn´t able to go. I chilled a few days more at Patrick’s place and then I got lucky because a friend went back to Austria by car and I could go with him. This is a short impression of my road trip in summer 2014, I made so many experiences and met many different and interesting people.

For my part I just can recommend everybody to pack his things and to go on a trip as fast as possible.
